# Do not use the generic bisection result as this issue's release history.
# dxc's preprocess option changed grammar twice (`P : Separate` -> `P : Flag` +
# `Fi`, 8bf2b087c / PR 4624, 2022-08-31). Releases <= v1.7.2207 reject `-Fi`
# with "Unknown argument". Before batch 012, run()'s `/Fi` spelling retry was
# SILENTLY DESTRUCTIVE on those releases: with
# `P : Separate`, `-P repro.hlsl /Fi preprocessed.i` makes repro.hlsl the
# OUTPUT file and overwrites it with preprocessed text, exit 0. The runner now
# probes in an isolated scratch copy and hard-fails input mutation, so the
# committed repro is protected. The generic command still cannot express both
# historical grammars, however. Release history therefore comes from
# manual-case-release-history.txt, which uses the spelling each release accepts.
#
# 1-2: the repro. Preprocess, then bring the preprocessed text back onto stdout
#      by compiling it with -Zi, which embeds the compiled file's source in
#      !dx.source.contents. `dxc -P` writes to a file, so nothing else puts the
#      artifact under test where a predicate can score it.
# 3-4: the same chain over control-token-in-code.hlsl, which differs from the
#      repro in exactly one way: `keepme3044` also appears as a code
#      identifier. Its presence is a required clause of match.json, so a broken
#      instrument scores no-match instead of manufacturing a clean absence.
-P repro.hlsl -Fi preprocessed.i
-T ps_6_0 -E main -Zi preprocessed.i
-P control-token-in-code.hlsl -Fi control-token-in-code.i
-T ps_6_0 -E main -Zi control-token-in-code.i
